riddle.q: The more you take, the more you *leave behind.* What am I?
What gets *wetter* the more it dries?
What has *keys* but can't open locks?
What has *hands* but can't clap?
What has to be *broken* before you can use it?
I'm *tall* when I'm young and *short* when I'm old. What am I?
What has a *neck* but no head?
What goes *up* but never comes *down?*
What has lots of *teeth* but can't bite?
What can you *catch* but not throw?
What has *one eye* but can't see?
What *runs* but never walks, has a *mouth* but never talks?
The more of me there is, the *less you see.* What am I?
Which word is spelled *wrong* in every dictionary?
I have *cities* but no houses, *forests* but no trees. What am I?
It's *yours*, but other people use it more than you. What is it?
What travels *around the world* but stays in a corner?
What has a *head* and a *tail* but no body?
Forwards I'm *heavy*, backwards I'm *not.* What am I?
What gets *bigger* the more you take away from it?

quiz.why: On Venus, the Sun rises in the west.
quiz.cap: Venus rotates the opposite way to most planets, so its Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

quiz.why: It covers about a third of Earth.
quiz.cap: The Pacific is bigger than all of Earth's land put together.

quiz.q: How many bones does an *adult* human have?
quiz.cap: Babies are born with around 300 bones. Many fuse together as we grow, leaving 206.
Diamond is carbon atoms bonded in an incredibly strong 3D lattice. That's why it can cut almost anything.

quiz.q: Which planet is *closest* to the Sun?
quiz.why: A year there lasts just 88 days.
quiz.cap: Mercury zips round the Sun in 88 Earth days. Yet Venus is hotter, thanks to its thick atmosphere.
Cheetahs can go from 0 to 100 km/h in about 3 seconds, but only for short sprints.
Au comes from the Latin "aurum". (Ag is silver, from "argentum".)

quiz.q: Which country has the *most* time zones?
quiz.cap: Thanks to territories from the Caribbean to the Pacific, France spans 12 time zones. Russia has 11. Did that catch you out?

quiz.q: What colour is a polar bear's *skin?*
quiz.cap: Polar bear skin is black and their hairs are transparent. They just look white because they scatter light.

quiz.q: What's the *longest* bone in your body?
quiz.cap: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.

quiz.q: How many minutes are in *one day?*
quiz.cap: 24 hours × 60 minutes = 1,440 minutes. Make them count.

quiz.why: 1 isn't prime. 2 is the only even one.
quiz.cap: A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 only has one, so it doesn't count. That makes 2 the smallest (and the only even) prime.
Jupiter is so big that more than 1,300 Earths would fit inside it.

quiz.q: How many sides does a *hexagon* have?
quiz.why: Just like the cells in a honeycomb.
quiz.cap: Bees build hexagons because they tile perfectly and use the least wax for the space.
Plants take in carbon dioxide and use sunlight to make sugar, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

fact.cap: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, one pumps it round the body. The blood is blue because it uses copper, not iron, to carry oxygen.
Botanically, a berry develops from a single flower's ovary with seeds inside. Bananas qualify. Strawberries don't.

fact.q: A day on Venus is longer than its
fact.cap: Venus spins so slowly that one rotation takes longer than a full trip around the Sun.

fact.more: Their *taste sensors* are on their legs.
fact.cap: When a butterfly lands on a leaf, it can taste whether it's the right plant to lay eggs on.
The unicorn has been on Scottish royal coats of arms for centuries, standing for purity and strength.

fact.q: A group of flamingos is called a
fact.cap: Other great ones: a parliament of owls and a crash of rhinos.
Wombats are the only known animals that produce cube-shaped poop. Scientists found their intestines shape it that way.

fact.q: A sloth can hold its breath for
fact.cap: Sloths can slow their heart rate right down, so they can hold their breath for up to 40 minutes.

fact.q: In summer, the Eiffel Tower grows by up to
fact.cap: Metal expands when it heats up, so on hot days the iron tower gets a little taller.
Sharks have been around for roughly 450 million years. The first trees appeared about 390 million years ago.

fact.q: Sealed honey can stay edible for
fact.cap: Honey has very little water and is naturally acidic, so bacteria struggle to survive in it.
The cells lining your stomach are replaced every few days, and a mucus layer protects them from the acid.
